subject: zap-coding-agent
title: 378 semantic unit tests plus an eval harness and 14 e2e scripts, none executed by any CI workflow
evidence: .github/workflows/build.yml:70-96 (steps are build/package/release only); grep 'cargo test' .github/ = 0 hits; security-audit.yml:23-24 runs only cargo-audit+cargo-deny
one_why: The tests are real property tests (grant-class cross-talk, trust-gate env handling, cache_control marking at src/llm_client/anthropic.rs:527) so a single cargo-test job on push would convert the subject's biggest paper strength into actual regression defense; today every claim of 'tested' is unenforced.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Compaction trigger projects the tokens of skills that WOULD be injected this turn, not just current context
evidence: src/session/turn.rs:74-93 (projected_skill_tokens computed before ctx_pct check), :121 (auto-compact at projected >= 90%), :107-119 (hard stop at 100% when budget set)
one_why: Fixes the classic hole where a window at '75%' plus a fat skill match overflows the model anyway: the same rank_and_truncate pass that builds the injection is run speculatively first, so the threshold sees the payload the model will actually receive.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Keyword-matched skills are ranked and truncated to a per-turn skill_token_budget, with the effective token cost shown per turn
evidence: src/skill_manager.rs:790-802 (match_skills_scoped with domain scope); src/session/turn.rs:148-158 (rank_and_truncate_skills to config.skill_token_budget), :382-386 (per-turn 'skills Nt' cost line)
one_why: Converges with the lazy-skill-loading cluster (kolega-code's budget idea, maki's index-only prompt); zap's unit is whole skill bodies per matched turn with a default 4000-token cap and visible accounting, which makes the injection decision debuggable turn by turn (skill_trace at turn.rs:160-170).

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Unconnected MCP servers occupy zero tool slots: one synthetic mcp_connect tool names them, and connecting is a model-initiated tool call
evidence: src/tools/mod.rs:221-244 (synthetic mcp_connect appended only when pending servers exist), :138 (load_mcp_lazy), tests :305-385
one_why: Lazy MCP without any search-tool machinery: N servers cost one tool definition instead of hundreds of schemas, and the model pays the connect cost only when a task actually needs that server -- a cheaper cousin of tool-search approaches.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Repo-local hooks.json and .mcp.json are inert until the directory is explicitly trusted (env / .zap/trusted marker / ~/.zap/trusted_dirs)
evidence: src/trust.rs:1-58 (three trust paths, canonicalized path compare), :73+ (unit tests incl. env-lock for parallel-safety)
one_why: Converges with pi's project-trust gate; the framing comment ('cloning and opening an untrusted repo cannot execute its hooks/servers') plus a one-line untrusted_hint() at the point of skip makes the gate discoverable instead of silent -- the skip-then-hint pattern is the portable part.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Two-tier substring patterns: hard-block list rejects even in Auto mode; destructive list forces a confirmation prompt even in Auto mode
evidence: src/tools/shell.rs:14 (BLOCKED_PATTERNS) and :97-115 (DESTRUCTIVE_PATTERNS with per-pattern reason strings), escalation wired at src/session/tools.rs:83
one_why: The interesting wrinkle over the standard denylist anti-pattern is the second tier: Auto mode is not blanket-auto, patterns like force-push or 'drop table' downgrade themselves to NeedsPrompt with a human-readable reason -- partial credit despite the whole thing being bypassable (which SECURITY.md:14-16 admits verbatim).

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: SECURITY.md grades each sandbox mode by whether it is a security boundary and calls its own denylist 'trivially bypassed'
evidence: docs/SECURITY.md:14-16 ('not a security boundary ... trivially bypassed with encoding, variable indirection'), :22-28 (off/workdir/container boundary table)
one_why: Converges with pi's honesty rung; zap goes further by labeling the weak middle mode (workdir = just current_dir, honestly marked 'Weak') instead of letting the word 'sandbox' imply enforcement -- an antipattern-inoculation doc other subjects should copy at the concept level.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Session 'always' grants work on tool-classes: approving edit_file grants write/batch/undo as one semantic unit while shell stays isolated
evidence: src/permission_manager.rs:13-21 (tool_grant_class), tests :250-280 (grant must fill the class and must NOT spill to shell)
one_why: Killstops the prompt-fatigue loop where four names for 'modify a file' each demand their own always-approval, while keeping the read/write-vs-shell boundary intact; the class + negative-spill test pair is the transferable artifact.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: SLM-mode loop breaker: exact equality of the previous round's {name:input} fingerprint set triggers a one-shot anti-loop nudge inside the next tool result, not an abort
evidence: src/session/turn.rs:500-537 (prev_call_fingerprints set compare, nudge appended to tool_msg)
one_why: Converges with crush's breaker but tuned for small chatty local models: identical-argument repetition means the model cannot gain new information, so the fix is an injected conclusion-prompt rather than killing the turn; cheap and falsifiable (set equality, one-shot).

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: MIT declared in Cargo.toml but no LICENSE file anywhere in the tree
one_why: A manifest SPDX field states intent but is not a grant of rights in most jurisdictions; until upstream adds the text, any reuse assessment must treat the repo as undeclared -- all findings here are concept-only and effort_for_us assumes clean-room implementation.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Per-turn task classifier swaps the provider/model for one turn from user-declared model_routes, then restores on exit -- including on every early-return path
evidence: src/session/routing.rs:12-27 (classify -> route -> save), src/session/turn.rs:68 (route_for_turn) with restore_routing called on budget-stop :119, error :369, and turn end :566
one_why: Routing granularity is the turn, not the session: cheap model for 'what is this repo', frontier model for refactor turns, and the save/restore discipline means a mid-turn error cannot strand the session on the wrong client -- the restore-on-all-paths pattern is what most routing designs get wrong.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: System prompt is chosen per turn class: casual greeting prompt (~12 tokens of persona), ~400-token SLM prompt, or full prompt -- with the compaction projection honoring the same class split
evidence: src/context_manager.rs:5-14 (build_casual_system_prompt, 'Saves ~6-8k tokens'), :20-46 (build_slm_system_prompt targeting ~400 tokens), src/session/turn.rs:78 (is_casual gates projected skill tokens to 0), :300-310 (casual sends last message only, no tools)
one_why: Beyond the lazy-skill corpus: the base prompt itself is tiered by detected turn class, so a greeting round-trip costs single-digit-tens of system tokens instead of thousands -- the compaction math and injection both respect the tier, which is what makes it safe rather than a context-losing hack.

subject: zap-coding-agent
title: Structured edit ledger (file, ops count, last turn) is rebuilt from session state and injected into the system prompt every turn, surviving sliding-window eviction
evidence: src/session/turn.rs:195-206 (ledger sorted by last_turn/ops_count, top 20, appended to effective_system); src/session/mod.rs:132,189 (ledger entries documented as surviving eviction)
one_why: Solves the post-compaction amnesia failure ('why did you touch that file?') with a deterministic, token-cheap projection instead of relying on the summarizer to preserve edit history -- the eviction-adjacent data gets its own non-LLM channel.
